key_insight: Entangled, intrinsically curved filaments can self-lock without friction through competing elastic shape-restoring forces and repulsive contact forces.
engineering_relevance: Filament geometry and bundle size offer design levers for cohesive assemblies and potentially stimuli-responsive materials that assemble or disassemble.
method: Analyze a friction-free model of intrinsically helical filament assemblies.
Test a generalized fracture criterion for spontaneous detangling.
Use experiments and simulations with frictional filaments to probe elastic self-locking.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports self-locking or soliton-like detanglement depending on filament number and preferred shape, including bundled structures that cannot self-lock at any friction level.
watch_item: Self-locking is geometry-dependent; friction alone cannot compensate for all filament shapes and bundle configurations.
paper_title: No friction required: Self-locking in entangled assemblies of curved filaments
